title: Repeat Visitor
statement: A museum scanner logs a badge ID each time a visitor enters. Return true if any badge was scanned more than once today.

approaches.name: HashMap / HashSet
approaches.label: best
approaches.why: One pass; a set answers "seen before?" in O(1) on average, so the first repeat is found right away.

approaches.name: Sort, then scan
approaches.label: valid
approaches.why: Repeats end up side by side, so one scan finds them. Correct, but sorting costs more than one pass.

approaches.name: Nested loops
approaches.label: valid
approaches.why: Correct, but 100,000 scans means about 5 billion comparisons.

approaches.name: Single pass
approaches.hint: One loop with a running value
approaches.label: unsuitable
approaches.why: A single running value cannot remember every badge seen so far.

title: Two Gifts, Exact Budget
statement: You have a gift card worth exactly budget. Prices are listed in no particular order. Return the positions of two different gifts whose prices add up to the budget, or [-1, -1].

approaches.name: HashMap / HashSet
approaches.label: best
approaches.why: For each price, look up budget − price among the prices already seen, with their positions.

approaches.name: Nested loops
approaches.label: valid
approaches.why: Checks every pair. Correct, but slow for 100,000 prices.

approaches.name: Sort, then scan
approaches.label: valid
approaches.why: Works if each price keeps its original position while sorting; searching the sorted list for the pair is taught in Level 12.

approaches.name: Single pass
approaches.hint: One loop with a running value
approaches.label: unsuitable
approaches.why: One running value cannot tell which earlier price completes the pair.

title: Class Election Winner
statement: Each student writes one name on a ballot. Return the name with the most votes. If names tie, return the one that comes first alphabetically.

approaches.name: HashMap / HashSet
approaches.label: best
approaches.why: Count each name in a map, then pick the highest count, breaking ties by name.

approaches.name: Sort, then scan
approaches.label: valid
approaches.why: After sorting, equal names sit together, so one scan counts each run. Correct, and ties already come in alphabetical order.

approaches.name: Nested loops
approaches.label: valid
approaches.why: Counting every name by scanning the whole list again is correct, but slow for 100,000 ballots.

approaches.name: Single pass
approaches.hint: One loop with a running value
approaches.label: unsuitable
approaches.why: Keeping only a current leader fails: a name seen early can overtake later, and you no longer know its count.
